text:
oncall: seeing a burst of apiserver 503s in ap-northeast1 starting ~17:41 UTC, controller-manager is in a restart loop on 3 masters. GPU attach queue spiked at the same time. anyone on this?

jordan: oncall can you paste the apiserver logs / graph link? also is etcd leader flipping?

oncall: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/controlplane/controlplane-overview?orgId=1&var-region=ap-northeast1 -> apiserver 5xx spike here, attach_rate metric jumps. logs show a bunch of TLS handshake errors then `io timeout`. snippet:```apiserver[kube-apiserver]: E0417 17:41:05.123 server.go:123] http2: panic serving 10.0.1.12:56324: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.0.1.12:56324: write: connection reset by peer```

linh: could be SNAT conntrack exhaustion on the NAT gateways — we've hit that before during large attach storms. can someone check `conntrack -L | wc -l` and NAT SNAT pool usage?

oncall: running conntrack check on a couple nodes now, one node at 115k entries (conntrack max 128k). also seeing many ESTABLISHED->TIME_WAIT churn from kube-proxy health probes.

marta: the provisioner team pushed a change 17:35 UTC that removed a label filter so it started trying to attach GPUs to older nodepools. i suspect a misrouted attach flood. tagging @jordan for rollout rollback?

jordan: rollback initiated for provisioner config (helm rollback provisioner v2 -> v1) — will take 60s. I also bumped apiserver replicas from 3 -> 5 in the controlplane ASG to absorb fanout.

oncall: deploy-bot: deploy provisioner v1 rolled back by jordan at 17:43:12 UTC :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: apiserver ASG scale request accepted (3 -> 5) by jordan at 17:44:00 UTC :gear:

linh: quick mitigation: add a temporary conntrack sysctl bump on gateways: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and drop TCP keepalive timeout to help clear TIME_WAIT faster. doing that now on edge-nat-1 nodes.

oncall: after rollback + conntrack bump we see apiserver 5xx tailing off, attach_rate back down to baseline. controller-manager restarts reduced from 4/min -> 0.5/min.

marta: follow-ups: 1) revert provisioner change with a test that validates label filters, 2) add rate limit on attach attempts in the provisioner (suggest `--attach-rate-limit=150`), 3) add nat SNAT pool autoscaling alert and playbook.
jordan: filing infra-ticket INF-4721 with the above action items and cost impact estimate (excess LB/NAT bandwidth during storm).

oncall: temporary pager clear, monitoring for 30m to ensure stable. thanks all. :thumbsup:
